question: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius of base 7 cm and height 10.2 cm.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a cylinder is directly proportional to its base area and height.

Base Area = πr² = (22 ÷ 7) × 7² = 154 cm².

Volume = Base Area × Height = 154 × 10.2

Volume = 154 × (10 + 0.2) = 1540 + 30.8 = 1570.8 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1570.8 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Volume of Cylinder = πr²h

**Given:**

⇒ Radius of the base (r) = 7 cm

⇒ Height of the cylinder (h) = 10.2 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a cylinder (V) = π × r² × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ V = (22 ÷ 7) × (7)² × 10.2

⇒ V = (22 ÷ 7) × 49 × 10.2

⇒ V = 22 × 7 × 10.2

⇒ V = 154 × 10.2

⇒ V = 1570.8 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1570.8 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder

The lateral area excluding the top and bottom circular bases. Formula: CSA = 2πrh

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

The total area covering the curved surface and the two solid circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πr(r + h)

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume. Formula: V = (1 ÷ 3)πr²h
